content: Terconazole vaginal cream and suppositories are prescribed to treat fungal and yeast infections of the vagina. In some cases, this medication may be prescribed for other uses. If you have questions about its use, consult your doctor or pharmacist for more information. Terconazole is available as a cream or suppository, both of which are designed to be inserted into the vagina. Typically, it is used once daily at bedtime for either 3 or 7 days, depending on your doctor’s instructions. Follow the directions on your prescription label carefully, and ask your doctor or pharmacist if you have any questions. Use the medication exactly as directed. Do not use more or less of it, or use it more frequently than prescribed. To use the vaginal cream or suppositories, follow these steps: For the cream, fill the special applicator provided with the cream to the level indicated. For the suppository, unwrap it, moisten it with lukewarm water, and place it on the applicator as shown in the accompanying instructions. Lie on your back with your knees drawn upward and spread apart. Insert the applicator high into your vagina (unless you are pregnant). Then, push the plunger to release the medication. If you are pregnant, insert the applicator gently. If you encounter resistance or difficulty inserting it, stop and contact your doctor. Withdraw the applicator. After each use, pull the applicator apart and clean it thoroughly with soap and warm water. Wash your hands promptly to prevent spreading the infection. The dose should be applied when you lie down to go to bed. The medication works best if you remain lying down after application, except to wash your hands. You may choose to wear a sanitary napkin to protect your clothing from stains, but do not use a tampon, as it will absorb the medication. Avoid douching unless instructed to do so by your doctor. Continue using terconazole even if you feel better. Do not stop using it without consulting your doctor. You should also continue using this medication during your menstrual period. Before using terconazole, inform your doctor and pharmacist if you are allergic to terconazole or any other drugs. Additionally, let them know about all prescription and nonprescription medications you are taking, especially antibiotics and vitamins. Inform your doctor if you have or have ever had issues with your immune system, HIV infection, AIDS, or diabetes. If you are pregnant, planning to become pregnant, or breastfeeding, notify your doctor. If you become pregnant while using terconazole, contact your doctor immediately, as this medication may harm the fetus. If you forget to use a dose, insert it as soon as you remember. However, if it is almost time for your next dose, skip the missed dose and continue with your regular dosing schedule. Do not insert a double dose to make up for a missed one. Terconazole may cause side effects. Mild side effects include headaches and missed menstrual periods. If these symptoms are severe or persistent, inform your doctor. Severe side effects include burning or irritation in the vagina when the cream or suppository is inserted, stomach pain, fever, or foul-smelling vaginal discharge. If you experience any of these, contact your doctor immediately. Serious side effects can be reported to the FDA’s MedWatch Adverse Event Reporting program online or by phone. Store this medication tightly closed in its original container and out of reach of children. Keep it at room temperature, away from excess heat and moisture (do not store it in the bathroom). Dispose of outdated or unneeded medication properly, and consult your pharmacist about the correct disposal method. Keep all appointments with your doctor. Terconazole is for external use only. Avoid getting the cream in your eyes or mouth, and do not swallow it. Do not swallow the suppositories. Refrain from sexual intercourse while using this medication. An ingredient in the cream may weaken certain latex products, such as condoms or diaphragms, so avoid using these products within 72 hours of applying the medication. Wear clean cotton underwear (or underwear with cotton crotches) rather than synthetic fabrics like nylon or rayon. Do not share your medication with others. If you have questions about refilling your prescription, ask your pharmacist. If your symptoms persist after completing the course of terconazole, contact your doctor.
